questions.prompt: The soldier praises both the general and the sword; the latter defends the body, the former the state.
questions.answer: Mīles et ducem et gladium laudat; hīc corpus, ille cīvitātem dēfendit.

questions.prompt: Themistocles sent a letter to the king in the following words.
questions.answer: Themistoclēs hīs verbīs epistulam ad rēgem mīsit.

questions.prompt: The famous Solon, wisest of all, gave just laws to the citizens.
questions.answer: Solōn ille, sapientissimus omnium, iūstās lēgēs cīvibus dedit.

questions.prompt: That fellow, seized by greed, betrayed his own friends.
questions.answer: Iste homō, avāritiā captus, amīcōs suōs prōdidit.

questions.prompt: We praise the man who saved the besieged city.
questions.answer: Eum virum laudāmus quī urbem obsessam servāvit.

questions.prompt: I am not such a man as to be easily frightened by dangers.
questions.answer: Nōn is sum quī perīculīs facile terrear.

questions.prompt: This is virtue, not to abandon one's country in danger.
questions.answer: Haec est virtūs, patriam in perīculō nōn dēserere.

questions.prompt: I admire Cicero and Cato; the latter was stern, the former eloquent.
questions.answer: Cicerōnem et Catōnem admīror; hīc sevērus, ille disertus fuit.

questions.prompt: The famous Hannibal, leader of the Carthaginians, crossed the Alps with his army.
questions.answer: Hannibal ille, dux Poenōrum, Alpēs cum exercitū superāvit.

questions.prompt: We will give rewards to those who bravely drove back the enemy.
questions.answer: Eīs praemia dabimus quī hostēs fortiter reppulērunt.

questions.prompt: The king gave the envoys the following orders: that they surrender the city without delay.
questions.answer: Rēx lēgātīs haec mandāta dedit: urbem sine morā trāderent.

questions.prompt: Our forces are not such as to withstand so great an enemy.
questions.answer: Nōn eae sunt cōpiae nostrae quae tantum hostem sustineant.

questions.prompt: I often read Virgil and Horace; the latter wrote shorter poems, the former greater ones.
questions.answer: Vergilium et Horātium saepe legō; hīc breviōra, ille maiōra carmina scrīpsit.

questions.prompt: This is wisdom, to yield to the occasion and to control one's anger.
questions.answer: Ea est sapientia, temporī cēdere et īram regere.

questions.prompt: He was not the sort of man to abandon a friend in adversity.
questions.answer: Is nōn erat quī amīcum in rēbus adversīs relinqueret.

questions.prompt: Remember this, that no one attains glory without toil.
questions.answer: Illud memoriā tenēte, nēminem sine labōre glōriam adipīscī.

questions.prompt: The famous Alexander the Great subdued the whole world by arms.
questions.answer: Alexander ille Magnus tōtum orbem armīs subēgit.

questions.prompt: Peace and war are set before the state; the latter brings ruin, the former safety.
questions.answer: Pāx et bellum cīvitātī prōpōnuntur; hoc ruīnam, illa salūtem affert.

questions.prompt: I consider those citizens happy who obey the laws.
questions.answer: Eōs cīvēs beātōs habeō quī lēgibus pārent.

questions.prompt: The orator spoke in the following manner: that no one sins unpunished.
questions.answer: Ōrātor hunc in modum locūtus est: nēminem impūne peccāre.

questions.prompt: My ability is not such that I can bear so great a burden.
questions.answer: Nōn ea est facultās mea ut tantum onus sustineam.

questions.prompt: Wealth and virtue are offered to the young man; the latter brings lasting praise, the former brief pleasure.
questions.answer: Adulēscentī dīvitiae et virtūs offeruntur; haec perpetuam laudem, illae brevem voluptātem afferunt.

questions.prompt: Cicero wrote to his brother in the following words, that the republic was in the gravest danger.
questions.answer: Cicerō frātrī hīs verbīs scrīpsit, rem pūblicam in maximō perīculō esse.

questions.prompt: I understand this, that the minds of all citizens are turned toward the new consul.
questions.answer: Illud intellegō, omnium cīvium animōs ad novum cōnsulem conversōs esse.

questions.prompt: That fellow, driven by envy, accused the innocent man before the judges.
questions.answer: Iste homō, invidiā incitātus, innocentem apud iūdicēs accūsāvit.

questions.prompt: The famous Scipio, conqueror of Carthage, was honored by the whole people.
questions.answer: Scīpiō ille, victor Carthāginis, ā tōtō populō honōrātus est.

questions.prompt: I loved Fabius, the man who by delaying restored the state.
questions.answer: Fabium, eum quī cūnctandō rem restituit, dīlēxī.

questions.prompt: I am not such a woman as to be moved by empty threats.
questions.answer: Nōn sum ea quae inānibus minīs commovear.

questions.prompt: He did not perceive—a thing which he will soon regret—that many witnesses remained.
questions.answer: Nōn sēnsit, id quod mox dolēbit, multōs testēs superesse.

questions.prompt: No speeches delight me except those of Cicero.
questions.answer: Nūllae mē ōrātiōnēs dēlectant nisi Cicerōnis.

questions.prompt: He had served in the army of Caesar and afterward in that of Pompey.
questions.answer: In exercitū Caesaris et posteā in Pompeī mīlitāverat.

questions.prompt: The general threatened the captives with imprisonment, and that too everlasting.
questions.answer: Dux captīvīs vincula, et ea sempiterna, minātus est.

questions.prompt: A brave man, whom we also call wise, fears no dangers.
questions.answer: Vir fortis, quem eundem sapientem appellāmus, nūlla perīcula timet.

questions.prompt: On that very day the enemy attacked the camp.
questions.answer: Eō ipsō diē hostēs castra oppugnāvērunt.

questions.prompt: The gates opened of their own accord, and the terrified guards fled.
questions.answer: Portae ipsae sē aperuērunt, et perterritī custōdēs fūgērunt.

questions.prompt: By mere fear the citizens were driven from the walls of the city.
questions.answer: Ipsō terrōre cīvēs ā moenibus urbis pulsī sunt.

questions.prompt: The wise man cannot restrain himself when he is driven by anger.
questions.answer: Sapiēns sē ipse continēre nōn potest, cum īrā incitātur.

questions.prompt: The soldiers feared that the leader would desert them and flee to the enemy.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs timuērunt nē dux ab ipsīs dēscīsceret et ad hostēs fugeret.

questions.prompt: Men ought to bear most calmly those things which have been brought about by their own fault.
questions.answer: Hominēs aequissimē ferre dēbent ea quae ipsōrum culpā contracta sunt.

questions.prompt: The consul himself was present in person and encouraged the wavering ranks.
questions.answer: Cōnsul ipse aderat et dubitantēs ōrdinēs cohortābātur.

questions.prompt: That wretched fellow squandered his inheritance and later begged for bread.
questions.answer: Iste miser patrimōnium dissipāvit et posteā pānem mendīcābat.

questions.prompt: The king answered in the following words, that he would never surrender the citadel.
questions.answer: Rēx hīs verbīs respondit, sē numquam arcem trāditūrum esse.

questions.prompt: A great grief crushed the mother, which likewise befell the father.
questions.answer: Magnus dolor mātrem oppressit, quod idem patrī contigit.

questions.prompt: We reached the very bank of the river, where the enemy were awaiting us.
questions.answer: Ad ipsam flūminis rīpam pervēnimus, ubi hostēs nōs exspectābant.

questions.prompt: We honored the man who freed the captives from cruel bondage.
questions.answer: Eum quī captīvōs ā crūdēlī servitūte līberāvit honōrāvimus.

questions.prompt: Caesar and Pompey waged war; the latter fled, the former conquered.
questions.answer: Caesar et Pompēius bellum gessērunt; hīc fūgit, ille vīcit.

questions.prompt: The famous Socrates used to teach young men wisdom in the forum.
questions.answer: Sōcratēs ille iuvenēs sapientiam in forō docēbat.

questions.prompt: I understand this, that fortune favors the brave.
questions.answer: Illud intellegō, fortūnam fortēs adiuvāre.

questions.prompt: That fellow scorns the laws and fears no punishment.
questions.answer: Iste homō lēgēs contemnit et nūllam poenam timet.

questions.prompt: I honored Fabius, the man who by delaying restored the state.
questions.answer: Fabium, eum quī cūnctandō rem pūblicam restituit, honōrāvī.

questions.prompt: You are not such a man as to betray your country.
questions.answer: Nōn is es quī patriam prōdās.

questions.prompt: He conquered the enemy in a single battle — a thing which no one had hoped.
questions.answer: Hostēs, id quod nēmō spērāverat, ūnō proeliō vīcit.

questions.prompt: The plays of Terence delight me, but not those of Plautus.
questions.answer: Terentī fābulae mē dēlectant, sed nōn Plautī.

questions.prompt: Cicero, whom we also call the father of his country, saved Rome.
questions.answer: Cicerō, quem eundem patrem patriae appellāmus, Rōmam servāvit.

questions.prompt: He bore his exile, and that too undeserved, with a calm mind.
questions.answer: Exsilium, et id immeritum, aequō animō tulit.

questions.prompt: On that very night the leader led his forces across the river.
questions.answer: Eā ipsā nocte dux cōpiās trāns flūmen dūxit.

questions.prompt: The gates opened of their own accord, and the city was taken by mere terror.
questions.answer: Portae sē ipsae aperuērunt, et urbs ipsō terrōre capta est.

questions.prompt: The wise man cannot always control himself in anger.
questions.answer: Sapiēns sē ipse in īrā semper continēre nōn potest.

questions.prompt: The leader feared that his soldiers would desert him and cross over to the enemy.
questions.answer: Dux timēbat nē mīlitēs ab ipsō dēscīscerent et ad hostēs trānsīrent.

questions.prompt: The consul spoke these words: that the fatherland must be defended by all.
questions.answer: Cōnsul haec verba dīxit: patriam ab omnibus dēfendendam esse.

questions.prompt: This is true glory, to have deserved well of the republic.
questions.answer: Haec est vēra glōria, dē rē pūblicā bene meruisse.

questions.prompt: The famous Homer sang of the wrath of Achilles and the fall of Troy.
questions.answer: Homērus ille īram Achillis et excidium Trōiae cecinit.

questions.prompt: This soldier, whom we likewise call brave, never fled from battle.
questions.answer: Hīc mīles, quem eundem fortem vocāmus, numquam ex proeliō fūgit.

questions.prompt: The virtue of our ancestors was greater than that of their descendants.
questions.answer: Māiōrum virtūs māior fuit quam posterōrum.

questions.prompt: Riches and wisdom are sought by men; the latter is lasting, the former fleeting.
questions.answer: Dīvitiae et sapientia ab hominibus petuntur; haec perpetua, illae cadūcae sunt.
